candidates.title: The Stars That Would Not Stay Sharp
story_beats: At the snowy meadow, fox and rabbit discovered the observatory telescope showed trembling stars despite a clear sky before the library opened, leaving the visiting readers waiting.
Fox attempted an immediate fix, but they cleaned the lens and refocused it but the stars kept wobbling; rabbit stopped the attempt before the situation worsened.
Rabbit examined the evidence and realized warm air from a roof exhaust vent crossed the telescope's line of sight; together they revised their plan rather than repeating the mistake.

With the visiting readers watching, they redirected the warm exhaust away from the viewing slit and checked the stars again, then explained the clue so their neighbors could prevent the problem next time.

candidates.title: The Runners Who Never Crossed the Line
story_beats: At the snowy meadow, fox and rabbit discovered the charity race clock failed to record runners who clearly crossed the finish before the library opened, leaving the visiting readers waiting.
Fox attempted an immediate fix, but they replaced the runners' timing tags but the missed finishes continued; rabbit stopped the attempt before the situation worsened.
Rabbit examined the evidence and realized a metal banner frame beside the finish line was interfering with the timing antenna; together they revised their plan rather than repeating the mistake.

With the visiting readers watching, they moved the banner frame away and verified the gate using test tags before reopening, then explained the clue so their neighbors could prevent the problem next time.

candidates.title: The Bags That Split at One Corner
story_beats: At the snowy meadow, fox and rabbit discovered every paper bag from the market stall tore at the same folded corner before the library opened, leaving the visiting readers waiting.
Fox attempted an immediate fix, but they used thicker paper but the next stack split along the same line; rabbit stopped the attempt before the situation worsened.
Rabbit examined the evidence and realized the bag-folding machine was scoring one crease too deeply and weakening the paper; together they revised their plan rather than repeating the mistake.
With the visiting readers watching, they adjusted the scoring wheel and tested the new bags with weighted parcels, then explained the clue so their neighbors could prevent the problem next time.
